insights.headline: MCX gold rebounds Rs 8,345 in two sessions as the dollar eases, but Fed hike bets cap the rally
insights.summary: MCX gold rose nearly Rs 4,000 per 10 g on Friday to an intraday high of Rs 1,26,251, rebounding Rs 8,345 from Wednesday's low and set to snap a two-week losing streak as tech stocks steadied and the dollar eased. Spot gold held near $3,675 and silver near $44, with COMEX gold up 4% to $3,708. Markets still price a near-certain December Fed hike, and analysts warn rallies face resistance near $3,700, with HSBC flagging $3,400 if equities slide again.
points: MCX gold rose nearly Rs 4,000 per 10 g on Friday to Rs 1,26,251, rebounding Rs 8,345 from Wednesday's low and set to snap a two-week losing streak.
Spot gold held near $3,675 and silver near $44, with COMEX gold up 4% to $3,708 and silver futures up 10% to $44.24.
SEBI will let foreign portfolio investors trade physically settled non-agri commodity derivatives from June 2027, opening MCX to more overseas flow.
A softer dollar and steadier tech stocks lifted bullion, but a December Fed hike is fully priced and analysts warn rallies face resistance near $3,700.
India's forex reserves fell $4.44 billion to $700.90 billion in the week ended Nov 20 as gold reserves dropped $4.10 billion.

brief.headline: Gold rebounds to $3,664 as dollar eases; Fed hike caps gains
brief.summary: Gold rose nearly 3% to $3,664 and silver 6% to $44.18, with MCX gold at Rs 1,25,151 per 10 g, as the dollar eased.

bullets.text: Silver outpaced gold on the rebound, with COMEX gold up 4% to $3,708 and silver futures up 10% to $44.24.
A softer dollar and calmer equities lifted bullion, Reuters says, but December Fed hike bets cap the rally; HSBC warns $3,400 is at risk.
Watch: ISM manufacturing PMI on Monday at 20:30 IST, then US jobs and the RBI policy decision on Dec 4, ahead of the Fed on Dec 9.

trending.title: MCX gold snaps back Rs 8,345
trending.summary: MCX gold rebounded Rs 8,345 from Wednesday's low as a softer dollar and steadier tech stocks steadied bullion, with silver surging too.

trending.title: Fed hike bets still cap the rally
trending.summary: Markets price a near-certain December hike after hot October PCE, and analysts warn rallies face resistance until the Dec 8-9 Fed meeting.

trending.title: Silver's rebound, still bearish underneath
trending.summary: Silver led the rebound but analysts call it short-covering in a thin market, with spot still far below January's record and rallies vulnerable.

trending.title: SEBI opens commodity derivatives to FPIs
trending.summary: Foreign portfolio investors will be able to trade physically settled non-agri commodity derivatives from June 2027, widening overseas access to MCX.

trending.title: India buys the dip; RBI's gold pile shrinks
trending.summary: Indian and Chinese demand revived as prices fell, while the RBI's gold reserves lost $4.10 billion in value and it moved 60 tonnes home this year.

items.title: MCX gold prices rebound over ₹8,300 in two sessions, set to snap 2-week losing streak; what lifted sentiment?
items.summary: MCX gold rose nearly Rs 4,000 per 10 g on Friday to an intraday high of Rs 1,26,251, Mint reports, rebounding Rs 8,345 from Wednesday's low and set to snap a two-week losing streak as steadier tech stocks and a softer dollar lifted sentiment; MCX silver surged Rs 9,000 per kg to Rs 1,54,804.

items.title: COMEX Gold Surges 4% to $3,708, MCX Gold Crosses ₹1.26 Lakh; COMEX Silver Futures Jumps 10%
items.summary: COMEX gold futures jumped 4% to $3,708.40 on Friday, extending the rebound from a 52-week low, while MCX gold rose 3.2% to an intraday high of ₹1,26,251 per 10 g. COMEX silver futures surged over 10% to $44.24 an ounce as risk appetite returned across Asian markets and Chinese stocks rallied.

items.title: Gold rebounds from one-year low as AI jitters ease
items.summary: Spot gold rose 1.6% to $3,622.91 on Friday, rebounding from its lowest since September 2025 as a US holiday lull calmed AI-driven market jitters, Reuters reports; bullion is up 2.7% on the week, silver climbed 4.6% to $43.40, and China's net gold imports via Hong Kong hit their highest since April.

items.title: Gold Price Forecast: Fed Rate Hike Bets Threaten the Latest Rebound
items.summary: Gold rebounded to $3,674.60 but stays below the former $4,000-$4,200 support zone, FXEmpire reports, with the dollar pulling back from a near 20-month high near $104.57; markets have fully priced a December Fed hike and a 66% chance of a 50-basis-point move in January.

items.title: Silver Price Forecast: Why I Remain Bearish Despite the Sharp Rally
items.summary: Silver's sharp rebound looks like short-covering in a thin holiday market, FXEmpire says, with spot near $44 but still down about 17% from a year ago and two-thirds below January's $121.67 record; rallies stay vulnerable near $45 and $48 while a December Fed hike is fully priced.

items.title: Gold's $3,750 ceiling: Analyst says a hawkish Fed "would cap Gold rallies"
items.summary: Gold is back above $3,600 and heading for a weekly gain after bouncing from a 15-month low near $3,425, FXStreet reports, but analysts say a hawkish Fed would cap rallies below $3,750; $3,500 must hold for the recovery to last, with the Fed's Dec 8-9 meeting the key test.

items.title: HSBC flags $3,400 as gold's next big test and says it is too early to call a bottom
items.summary: HSBC warns it is too early to call an end to gold's slide, InvestingLive reports, with further equity weakness able to push gold through major support at $3,400 an ounce; the bank sees limits to the selloff, while Saxo's Ole Hansen says gold's slide from its record looks overdone.

items.title: Gold slips, silver gains as Fed rate hike expectations persist in holiday trading - Kitco PM Report
items.summary: Spot gold eased in thin Thanksgiving trading as expectations of further Federal Reserve rate hikes and a firm dollar kept buyers cautious, Kitco reports, while silver edged higher. Gold traded near $3,565.50 an ounce, down 0.63%, and silver near $41.42, up 0.33%. Markets price a 99.4% chance of a December hike after hot October PCE data showed core inflation at 3.3%.

items.title: Gold Rebounds for the Week, but Fed Rate Hike Fears Keep Bears in Control
items.summary: Gold is set for a weekly rebound after bouncing from a 15-month low, Investing.com reports, but Fed rate-hike fears keep bears in control as markets price a near-certain December hike ahead of the Dec 8-9 FOMC meeting.

items.title: Gold price tracker, Nov 27: MCX gold jumps over ₹1.25 lakh, silver prices rally 5.5%
items.summary: MCX gold surged 2.35% to an intraday high of ₹1,25,151 per 10 g and silver jumped 5.5% to ₹1,53,954 per kg on Friday, Upstox reports, as value buying continued after the metals fell to around 14-month lows. COMEX gold traded 2.7% higher at $3,632 and silver 8.3% higher at $43.42, while jewellery stocks including Titan and Kalyan rose and the gold-silver ratio fell to $82.53.

items.title: India's forex reserves fall $4.44 billion to $700.90 billion, says RBI
items.summary: India's forex reserves fell $4.44 billion to $700.90 billion in the week ended November 20, RBI data shows, with gold reserves down $4.10 billion to $94.52 billion as lower bullion prices cut their value; foreign currency assets eased $266 million to $583.19 billion.

items.title: Sebi allows FPIs to trade in physically settled non-agri commodity derivatives
items.summary: SEBI will allow foreign portfolio investors to trade physically settled non-agricultural commodity derivatives from June 2027, Mint reports, revising a framework that restricted FPI participation to cash-settled non-agri contracts and indices.

items.title: Gold Rally Gains Momentum During Thanksgiving Holiday
items.summary: Gold's rebound gained momentum in thin Thanksgiving holiday trading, Investing.com's analysis notes, with bullion extending its recovery from a one-year low as risk appetite returned.

items.title: Spot gold up as futures rebound from 1-year low; wedding demand lends support
items.summary: Spot gold in India rose on Friday as MCX December gold touched ₹1,25,912 per 10 g, up 3%, and COMEX gold reached $3,683, with wedding-season demand and recycled-gold buying supporting prices. Informist notes jewellers offered no discounts as demand rose, though traders expect Fed hike bets to limit further gains.

items.title: Gold demand revives in India, China as price slide sparks bargain buying
items.summary: Gold demand in India and China revived this week as prices fell to their lowest in over a year, BusinessLine reports, with Indian domestic gold near ₹124,800 per 10 g after touching ₹1,17,906 and dealer premiums up to $19 an ounce as jewellers restock for the wedding season; China's net gold imports via Hong Kong hit their highest since April.

items.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG/USD surges to near $43.75 as US Dollar remains in corrective phase
items.summary: Silver extended its two-day recovery, surging almost 5% to near $43.75 as the dollar corrected from its near 20-month high of 104.57, FXStreet reports; ING notes a sustained dollar pullback may wait until the Fed meeting on December 9 or November CPI on December 10.

items.title: MCX market cap hits ₹1 trillion; stock rallies 11% in two days, up 77% YTD
items.summary: MCX shares hit a new high of ₹3,939.85 on Friday, taking the exchange's market value past ₹1 trillion, Business Standard reports; the stock is up 11% in two days and 77% so far this year, more than doubling from its 52-week low.

items.title: Titan, TBZ: Jewellery, gold financiers' stocks rise as bullion rebounds 2%
items.summary: Jewellery stocks rallied as bullion rebounded, Business Standard reports: Titan rose 3.7% to ₹4,805, Kalyan Jewellers gained 3.8% and PC Jeweller added 2%, tracking MCX gold's recovery to ₹1,24,787 per 10 g.

items.title: Rupee rally faces oil test; inflows, positive sentiment provide cushion
items.summary: The rupee's November rally, up 2.6% this month and Asia's best, faces a test from Brent crude above $96, though $16 billion of foreign equity inflows in November and improving sentiment towards Indian assets should cushion it, Reuters reports. The currency settled at 92.4450 to the dollar on Thursday, with the dollar index near a 22-month high.

items.title: India Bullion: Rise from lowest levels in over a year on short-covering
items.summary: Gold and silver futures on MCX recovered from their lowest levels in over a year on short-covering in thin Thanksgiving trading, Informist reports. The February gold contract ended at Rs 1,24,559 per 10 g, up 0.9%, and March silver at Rs 1,50,130 per kg, up 2.8%, even as a firm dollar and Fed hike expectations capped gains.

items.title: India’s central bank repatriates another 60 tonnes of gold in 2026 as share of FX reserves drops to 14.38%
items.summary: The RBI moved 60.08 tonnes of gold from overseas vaults to domestic storage in April–September 2026, Kitco reports, taking the domestic share to 84.05% of its 880.52 tonnes. The remaining 140.39 tonnes stay with the Bank of England and the BIS. Gold's share of forex reserves fell to 14.38% from 16.70% in March as total reserves rose to $737.78 billion.

items.title: Gold Prices Fall: Is India’s ₹23 Lakh Crore Gold Loan Market at Risk? | The Morning Brief Decode
items.summary: ET’s Morning Brief looks at the strain on India’s ₹23 lakh crore gold-loan market after gold’s sharp fall from its peak, with rising loan-to-value ratios squeezing borrowers and lenders. It examines whether lenders can auction pledged jewellery even without a missed repayment, why the RBI is concerned about repeat borrowers, and how exposed India’s biggest gold-loan companies are.

items.title: Gold demand remains strong despite price correction, says World Gold Council
items.summary: India's physical gold demand remains firm despite the correction, the World Gold Council's Sachin Jain said, with consumers buying on dips and ETF inflows recovering in the first half of November. Central banks bought more than 345 tonnes in the previous quarter, and gold ETF holdings were about 126 tonnes at end-October.

items.title: Gold Makes 17% Loss from Last Thanksgiving, Worst Since 2013
items.summary: Gold and silver held on to Wednesday's steep rebound from 15-month lows in thin Thanksgiving trading, BullionVault reports, with gold flat near $3,606 and silver around $41.50. Gold has lost 16.6% over 12 months, its worst such fall since the 28% crash of 2013, while silver is down 22.2% on the year. Fed funds futures price a 99.5% chance of a December hike.

items.title: Turkish central bank suspends its purchases of domestically produced gold, bankers say
items.summary: Turkey's central bank has suspended purchases of domestically produced gold until further notice, bankers told Reuters, without giving a reason. Turkey mines about 30 tonnes a year and the bank holds around 800 tonnes. The pause breaks a run of central-bank buying that has long supported gold.

items.title: Gold Falls Below $3,500 Mark as Russia Offloads 72 Tons Over Ten Straight Months, Becoming Biggest Selling Pressure
items.summary: Russia's central bank has cut its gold holdings for ten straight months, January to October, shedding about 72 tonnes — the most persistent selling among major official holders — as the Finance Ministry drew on the National Wealth Fund to cover the budget deficit, BigGo reports; Turkey, Russia and Azerbaijan's sovereign funds sold a combined net 166 tonnes through September.

items.title: PM Modi Says Gold Prices Fell After His Appeal: Does Govt Control Gold Rates or Does the International Market?
items.summary: PM Narendra Modi credited his appeal to avoid unnecessary gold purchases for the price fall, Juris Hour reports, noting 24-carat gold eased from about ₹15,250 a gram on May 9 to ₹12,523 on November 21. Prices are market-determined, the piece explains, though the government can move landed costs through customs duty — raised from 6% to 15% in May — while imports fell nearly 40% in April–October.
